Test Step 2 of the SFCC-236 build: two new components.

- `ZimmSizeChip` atom — overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSizeChip.css.ts}
- `ZimmSizeChipGroup` molecule — overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts}
- overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts (2 imports + 2 registry entries added)

## Context you need
This pair was renamed mid-build from `ZimmSizeSelectorOption`/`ZimmSizeSelector` to `ZimmSizeChip`/`ZimmSizeChipGroup` because an unrelated, unmerged branch (feature/SFCC-92) already claims `ZimmSizeSelector` for a completely different dropdown-based PDP component. Part of your job is confirming this rename was executed CLEANLY — no leftover "SizeSelector" naming anywhere (folder names, component names, recipe keys, comments, test descriptions, i18n message ids).

This pair mirrors `zimmColourSwatch` (atom, one clickable circle) / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` (molecule, the row + keyboard nav + roving tabindex) exactly, adapted for size chips instead of colour swatches. Read both exemplar pairs in full as your reference baseline.

## Required pass criteria — verify each independently

**ZimmSizeChip (atom):**
1. Renders a native `<button role="radio" aria-checked>` — not a div-with-onClick.
2. Four states, all distinguishable: Default (unselected/enabled), Selected (`aria-checked="true"`, distinct visual), Focus (uses the SAME `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` / `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` tokens already used by `zimmNavItem`/`zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `pageButton` — NOT invented new focus tokens), Disabled (real native `disabled` attribute).
3. Hover and Active/pressed are explicitly NOT implemented (no Figma spec for them) — confirm no `_hover`/`_active` rule exists in the recipe, and confirm there's a comment explaining why (mirroring `pageButton`'s precedent).
4. `onSelect(value)` fires on click when enabled; NEVER fires when disabled — verify this is actually tested (a disabled-button click that asserts onSelect was NOT called), not just assumed from `disabled` being set.
5. Hit area ≥ 24×24 (Figma spec is 28×28 — confirm the recipe doesn't shrink it via padding tricks).

**ZimmSizeChipGroup (molecule):**
6. `role="radiogroup"` with a real `aria-label`.
7. "One Size" case (exactly one value): renders NO button, NO radiogroup role at all — a plain non-interactive label. Confirm this is a genuinely different render branch, not a radiogroup that happens to have one item.
8. Arrow key navigation: all four directions (ArrowRight/Down move forward, ArrowLeft/Up move backward), wraps at both ends.
9. **Disabled chips are skipped by arrow navigation** — this is the trickiest case. Find the specific test with a disabled chip in the MIDDLE of the list and verify arrow nav actually jumps over it in both directions, not just that disabled chips can't be clicked.
10. Roving tabindex: exactly ONE chip has `tabIndex={0}` at any given moment; it updates as arrow-navigation changes the current chip. Tab should enter the group once and leave once.
11. `onSelect` fires with the correct value on BOTH click and arrow-navigation landing on a new chip — verify arrow navigation actually calls onSelect (not just moves DOM focus without triggering selection).
12. Composes `ZimmSizeChip` atoms for rendering — the group doesn't reimplement button/disabled/selected logic inline.

**Naming cleanliness:**
13. Case-insensitive search the entire diff for "SizeSelector" / "sizeSelector" / "size-selector" / "size_selector" in ANY form — component names, folder paths, recipe keys, comments, test `describe`/`it` strings, i18n message ids, JSDoc. Must be zero hits.
14. Recipe keys are literally `'ZimmSizeChip'` and `'ZimmSizeChipGroup'` — confirmed registered correctly in theme/components/index.ts, no collision with any base SFCC recipe name.

**Cross-cutting (same as always):**
15. `parts` array in each .css.ts exactly matches `styles.X` reads in that component's own index.tsx.
16. No bare Chakra token key anywhere; no raw hex/px/rem/em except an explicitly commented provisional/audit-allow exception (Implementer claims one: a 65px One Size label width — verify the comment is genuinely present and the audit script actually acknowledges it, don't just trust the claim).
17. TypeScript only, no unjustified `any`/non-null-assertion.

## The Implementer flagged one deviation for your review
Added an `isFocusable: boolean` prop to `ZimmSizeChip` that wasn't in the original spec, justified as "necessary to satisfy the group's roving-tabindex requirement — a wrapping element can't carry tabIndex, mirroring ZimmColourSwatch's identical required prop of the same name." Verify: (a) does `ZimmColourSwatch` really have this exact prop already, confirming precedent rather than invention, and (b) is it actually load-bearing for roving tabindex to work, or could the group have achieved the same result without adding a prop to the atom (e.g. by controlling tabIndex a different way)? This determines whether it's a justified, precedented necessity or unrequested scope creep.

## Falsification requirement
For at least TWO of the trickiest behaviours — disabled-chip-skipping in arrow nav (#9), and roving-tabindex-updates-with-arrow-nav (#10) — actually break the implementation on purpose, rerun the specific test, confirm it fails, then revert and reconfirm clean. This is the only way to know these tests are real evidence, not tautologies.

## Commands to run yourself
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```
Then run the FULL `npm run test` once and confirm the total against the last known-good baseline (before this step: 46 files / 691 tests after Step 1's commit — confirm the new total and that nothing pre-existing regressed).

Report CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE findings, UNIFORM vs ONE-OFF, what you tried to falsify, and what you could not verify.
